    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Accelerometer
    An acceleration sensor.
    AiThinkerEsp32CamBoard
    Selects the AI Thinker ESP32-CAM as @Board's target.
    ArduinoNanoEsp32Board
    Selects the Arduino Nano ESP32 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ESP32-S3, a dual-core Xtensa LX7, under Arduino's arduino:esp32 core.
    ArduinoNanoEsp32Image
    Generated from arduino-nano-esp32.png, rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, then displayed rotated 180 degrees.
    ArduinoPortentaH7Board
    Selects the Arduino Portenta H7's M7 core as @Board's target.
    ArduinoUnoBoardImage
    Generated by CoverImageGenerator from 2.png, rotated 90 degrees clockwise; do not edit by hand.
    ArduinoUnoR3Board
    Selects the classic Arduino UNO R3 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ATmega328P, an 8-bit AVR with 2 KB SRAM and 32 KB flash, under Arduino's arduino:avr core.
    ArduinoUnoR4WiFiBoard
    Selects the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi as @Board's target; has the onboard 12x8 LED matrix.
    ArucoMarker
    An ArUco fiducial marker from the DICT_4X4_50 dictionary: ids 0 to 49, each a 6x6 grid of cells whose outer ring is black and whose inner 4x4 cells encode the id.
    AsciiFont
    A 5x7 dot-matrix font covering the full printable ASCII range (32 space .. 126 ~), for printing arbitrary ASCII characters on the board's 12x8 LED matrix one at a time (two glyphs fit side by side: 5 + 1 gap + 5 = 11 of the 12 columns), and for the TFT shield's and the Grove OLED's text.
    Audio
    The Cardputer's built-in speaker.
    AvrEeprom
    Named-secret storage in the on-chip EEPROM of the UNO R3's ATmega328P (1 KB).
    Base64
    Bounded board implementation of the JDK MIME Base64 decoder used for a PEM private key.
    Base64.Decoder
    The decoder Base64.getMimeDecoder() returns; it decodes into a fixed 2 KiB buffer.
    BaseMotor
    A motor that runs forward or backward until it is stopped.
    Battery
    Battery readings exposed by a board.
    BaudRate
    Common baud rates exposed as named values by Juno's USB serial API.
    BluetoothLe
    The board's Bluetooth LE radio, as a central: it scans for a device that advertises a service, connects to it, and exchanges messages with one characteristic of that service.
    Bmi088
    Grove 6-Axis Accelerometer & Gyroscope (BMI088), accessed through I2C.
    Board
    Declares which Arduino board(s) a Juno program targets, e.g.
    BoardMemory
    Read-only introspection into Juno's arena allocator and the program's flash footprint.
    BoardModel
    Which board the program was compiled for.
    BoardSupported
    A type token for an Arduino board @Board can select as a compilation target.
    BufferedGyroscope
    A Gyroscope that keeps sampling its angular velocity at a fixed period in a buffer of its own, such as a FIFO on the sensor, so a reader that comes late still gets every sample since its previous read.
    BuiltInSensor
    A sensor built into the Technic Hub (88012).
    Camera
    A still-image camera that delivers each frame as JPEG bytes into a buffer the program owns.
    Certificate
    The board-side java.security.cert.Certificate: an X.509 certificate as the PEM text it was read from.
    CertificateException
    The board-side java.security.cert.CertificateException.
    CertificateFactory
    The board-side java.security.cert.CertificateFactory, for "X.509" certificates in PEM form, such as a CA certificate read from the SD card.
    Clock
    The board's monotonic clock.
    Cp210xSerial
    A Silicon Labs CP210x USB-to-UART bridge (CP2102, CP2104, ...) attached to a UsbHostShield: the chip on the RoboPeak RPLIDAR adapter and on many ESP32 and sensor boards.
    DataLoggerShield
    The AZDelivery Data Logger Module Data Recorder Shield: an SD card socket on the UNO's SPI pins, chip select on D10 (MOSI D11, MISO D12, SCK D13), plus a DS1307 real-time clock that this class does not drive.
    DCMotor
    A DC motor driven by a power level.
    Delay
    Timing operations recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.
    DetourPlanner
    Plans a mission's path for a Navigator and drives it around obstacles found on the way: the planner leJOS's PathFinder feeds a navigator through its WaypointListener, re-planning when the navigator says a leg ended at an obstacle, which leJOS leaves to the program.
    DifferentialDrive
    Coordinates two independently controlled motors as a differential drive.
    DifferentialDriveOdometry
    Updates a caller-owned pose from two wheel encoders and a heading sensor.
    DigitalOutput
    A zero-cost GPIO handle.
    DirectionFinder
    A source of the robot's direction in Cartesian degrees, which grow counter-clockwise, as a drive's positive turn does.
    Display
    A board display with basic drawing operations and text output.
    Drawable
    An image that draws itself on the TFT, centred over the current viewport.
    DriveGeometry
    Fixed geometry and encoder ratios for a two-wheel differential drive.
    Encoder
    Tachometer feedback for a motor or wheel.
    EncoderMotor
    A motor with basic position feedback: open-loop power control from DCMotor and the position reported by Encoder.
    Esp32Nvs
    Named-secret storage in the non-volatile storage (NVS) of an ESP32, for the boards that carry no secure element at all: the ESP32-family boards' own chip, and the ESP32-S3 coprocessor of the UNO R4 WiFi, whose core's Preferences library has the same API and carries each call to the coprocessor over the modem link (it needs the coprocessor firmware 0.4.1 or later; an older one leaves the store unavailable).
    GeneralSecurityException
    The board-side java.security.GeneralSecurityException.
    Gpio
    The board's GPIO pins.
    GroveAnalogGas
    Reads the analog SIG output of a Grove gas sensor connected to an analog Grove socket.
    GroveBaseShield
    Pin map for the passive Grove Base Shield for UNO.
    GroveDht11
    Reads Seeed's Grove Temperature & Humidity Sensor (DHT11).
    GroveDht22
    Reads Seeed's Grove Temperature and Humidity Sensor Pro using its DHT22 (AM2302) frame format.
    GroveGpsAir530
    Reads the Seeed Grove GPS Air530 over its one-way UART output.
    GroveInfraredEmitter
    A Grove infrared emitter module's signal connection.
    GroveInfraredReceiver
    A Grove infrared receiver module's signal connection.
    GroveLightV12
    Reads Seeed's analog Grove Light Sensor v1.2 as a LightDetector.
    GroveMotorDriverTb6612fng
    Seeed Grove I2C Motor Driver (TB6612FNG): two brushed DC-motor channels, A and B, on one Grove I2C socket.
    GroveOledSsd1315
    Grove 0.96-inch 128×64 yellow/blue OLED with an SSD1315 controller, connected over I2C.
    GrovePicoShield
    Pin map for Seeed's passive Grove Shield for Pi Pico v1.0 on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W.
    GrovePirMotion
    A Grove PIR motion sensor with a digital SIG output.
    GroveSoundV16
    Reads Seeed's analog Grove Sound Sensor (v1.6).
    GroveTemperatureV12
    Reads Seeed's Grove Temperature Sensor v1.2.
    GroveUltrasonicRanger
    Grove Ultrasonic Ranger (v1 or v2) on one Grove digital socket.
    GyroDifferentialPilot
    A Pilot over two EncoderMotors whose power the program sets directly, such as a Powered Up hub's, that closes both loops itself with a DirectionFinder, a GyroHeading for instance.
    GyroHeading
    A DirectionFinder over a Gyroscope: a virtual thread of its own reads the gyroscope's angular velocity every GyroHeading.SAMPLE_MILLIS and integrates it, so the direction keeps counting while the program waits on something else, such as an infrared round trip to an RCX.
    GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive
    A RegulatedDifferentialDrive that holds its heading with a DirectionFinder, such as a GyroHeading.
    Gyroscope
    The minimal contract for a gyroscope.
    Headers
    Request or response headers in Juno's bounded HTTP server subset.
    HeadingHoldController
    Applies a bounded proportional correction to keep a differential drive on a target heading.
    HttpClient
    The board-side java.net.http.HttpClient: sends a HttpRequest through the board's own NativeHttpRequests.
    HttpClient.Builder
    Builds a HttpClient.
    HttpClient.Redirect
    Whether a client follows the redirects it receives.
    HttpClient.Version
    The HTTP version a client asks for; the board always speaks HTTP/1.1.
    HttpContext
    A registered path prefix and its request handler.
    HttpExchange
    The bounded request view for the request currently dispatched by HttpServer.
    HttpHandler
    A JDK-shaped handler for one board-side HTTP request.
    HttpHeaders
    The board-side java.net.http.HttpHeaders: a response's headers, read from the client's header buffer.
    HttpMethod
    Named HTTP methods for matching against HttpExchange.getRequestMethod().
    HttpRequest
    The board-side java.net.http.HttpRequest: an immutable request for one URI, built once and sent as often as needed.
    HttpRequest.BodyPublisher
    A request body.
    HttpRequest.BodyPublishers
    The available HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.
    HttpRequest.Builder
    Builds a HttpRequest.
    HttpResponse<T>
    The board-side java.net.http.HttpResponse: the status code and body of the last request a client sent.
    HttpResponse.BodyHandler<T>
    Chooses how the body is delivered: HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofByteArray() or HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString().
    HttpResponse.BodyHandlers
    The available HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.
    HttpsConfigurator
    The TLS context used by a board HTTPS listener.
    HttpServer
    A bounded, single-connection subset of the JDK HttpServer, dispatched cooperatively by HttpServer.handleNext().
    HttpsServer
    HTTPS server counterpart.
    HttpStatus
    Named HTTP status codes, for HttpExchange.sendResponseHeaders and HttpResponse.statusCode(), which stay a plain int — these are ordinary compile-time-constant int fields, not a new intrinsic or type, exactly like Gpio.getOutput().
    HttpTimeoutException
    The board-side java.net.http.HttpTimeoutException: thrown by HttpClient.send(HttpRequest, HttpResponse.BodyHandler) when no response arrived within the request's timeout.
    HubColor
    A colour of a Powered Up hub's status LED, one of the eleven fixed colours the hub's LED protocol offers.
    HubPort
    Deprecated.
    Kept for one compatibility release.
    HX53InfraredEmitter
    An HX-53 infrared emitter using Juno's original software-carrier driver.
    HXM121InfraredReceiver
    An HX-M121 38 kHz demodulating infrared receiver.
    I2c
    Register access to an I2C peripheral on the board's primary I2C bus (Wire, the SDA/SCL pins).
    InetSocketAddress
    Board-side port-only form of java.net.InetSocketAddress used when binding a server listener.
    Infrared
    Serial bytes over modulated infrared light, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno and bit-banged on two plain pins, with no Arduino library.
    InfraredDriver
    Configures one of the two low-level infrared carrier implementations.
    InfraredDriver.Type
    The supported infrared carrier implementations.
    InfraredEmitter
    An infrared emitter module that configures the low-level transport required by its circuit.
    InfraredReceiver
    A demodulating infrared receiver module connected to one signal pin.
    JavaLogoImage
    Generated by CoverImageGenerator from 1.png; do not edit by hand.
    Json
    Entry point of Juno's JSON support, after JDK 28's jdk.incubator.json (JEP 540): Json.parse(String) validates a document once and returns its root JsonValue, navigated with get(String) and get(int) and read with asInt(), asDouble(), asString() and similar methods; JsonWriter produces JSON.
    JsonValue
    One value inside a JSON document, with the navigation and conversion methods of JDK 28's JsonValue (JEP 540): get(String), get(int), asInt(), asString(), toString().
    JsonWriter
    Writes JSON into a caller-owned byte[], placing commas and escaping strings, so request and response bodies need no hand-written quotes.
    KasaSmartPlug
    Local control and discovery for legacy TP-Link Kasa HS100 and HS110 plugs, over the JDK's own socket classes.
    Key
    Encoded board key.
    Keyboard
    A keyboard polled by the board program.
    KeyboardView
    A View that receives a key transition and the current Fn modifier state.
    KeyboardViewRouter
    The controller for a keyboard-driven board program using KeyboardView screens.
    KeyFactory
    The EC PKCS#8 subset of the JDK key factory.
    KeyManagementException
    The board-side java.security.KeyManagementException.
    KeyManager
    The board-side javax.net.ssl.KeyManager, only as the type of SSLContext.init(KeyManager[], TrustManager[], SecureRandom)'s first parameter: client certificates are not supported, so a program passes null.
    KeyManagerFactory
    Server identity subset of the JDK key manager factory.
    KeySpec
    Board counterpart of the JDK key specification marker.
    KeyStore
    The board-side java.security.KeyStore: an in-memory store of trusted certificates for a java.net.http client's SSLContext.
    KeyStoreException
    The board-side java.security.KeyStoreException.
    L298nMotor
    One brushed DC-motor channel of an L298N dual H-bridge module.
    LcdKeypadShield
    Driver for the common "LCD Keypad Shield" (a 16x2 HD44780-compatible character LCD in 4-bit mode, plus 5 buttons wired through a single resistor ladder into one analog pin), wired for its standard pinout as used by e.g.
    LightDetector
    A sensor that measures white-light level, independent of the device that provides it.
    LinkedMotors
    Two motors of one Powered Up hub paired into a virtual port, so one call drives both in sync, as for a two-motor vehicle.
    M5StackCardputerBoard
    Selects the M5Stack Cardputer as @Board's target.
    M5StackCardputerImage
    Generated from m5stack-cardputer.png, rotated 90 degrees clockwise and resized 3 percent smaller.
    MCU
    The selected board's onboard services.
    Mhs35TftDisplay
    Driver for the MHS-3.5-inch Raspberry Pi display: a 480x320 TFT on the Pi's 40-pin header with an ILI9486 controller and a resistive XPT2046 touch panel.
    MotionDetector
    A device that reports whether it has detected motion within its field of view.
    Mouse
    USB HID mouse control.
    MoveOutcome
    Why a Pilot's last move ended, and so why a Navigator's leg did.
    NanoConnectorCarrier
    Pin map for the passive Arduino Nano Connector Carrier (ASX00061): a microSD card slot on SPI, four Grove sockets and one Qwiic connector, all wired to ordinary Nano header pins.
    NativeAudio
    The M5Stack Cardputer's Audio, implemented by a compiler intrinsic over M5Cardputer.Speaker.
    NativeBattery
    The M5Stack Cardputer's battery, implemented by compiler intrinsics over M5Cardputer.Power.
    NativeBluetoothLe
    The board's BluetoothLe: the only instance, shared by MCU.getBluetoothLe().
    NativeBoardMemory
    The board's BoardMemory: each method is an intrinsic the compiler lowers to its runtime shim, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeBoardModel
    The board's own answer to MCU.getBoardModel().
    NativeCamera
    The AI Thinker ESP32-CAM's camera: NativeCamera.begin() and the native capture are intrinsics the compiler lowers to the core's esp_camera driver, so they have no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeClock
    The board's Clock: each method is a clock intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino core call, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeDigitalOutput
    The board's DigitalOutput factory: NativeDigitalOutput.of(int) is a GPIO intrinsic the compiler lowers to a pin mode and returns the pin number as the handle.
    NativeDisplay
    The M5Stack Cardputer's Display, implemented by compiler intrinsics over the Cardputer keyboard.
    NativeGpio
    The board's Gpio: each method is a GPIO intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino core call, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeHttpFeatures
    What a program does with java.net.http responses, answered when the program is linked.
    NativeHttpRequests
    The board's HTTP and HTTPS requests behind the board-side java.net.http client.
    NativeHttpSchemes
    Which URI schemes a program sends HTTP requests to, answered when the program is linked.
    NativeHttpServer
    The board's single-connection HTTP and HTTPS listener behind the board-side com.sun.net.httpserver API.
    NativeI2c
    The board's I2c: each method is an I2C intrinsic the compiler lowers to the core-bundled Wire library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeKeyboard
    The M5Stack Cardputer's Keyboard, implemented by compiler intrinsics over the Cardputer keyboard.
    NativeLedMatrix
    The board's built-in LED matrix as a Display: 12x8 on the UNO R4 WiFi, one color.
    NativeMouse
    The board's Mouse: each method is a USB HID intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino Mouse library (the core's USBHIDMouse on ESP32-S3 boards), so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeOnboardSdCard
    Owns the one card in the selected board's onboard microSD socket.
    NativeSdCard
    The card in a shield's SD socket: each method but NativeSdCard.begin() is an SD intrinsic the compiler lowers to the SdFat library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeSecretStore
    The selected board's secret store, opened on first use and shared after that.
    NativeSpi
    The board's Spi bus: each method is an SPI intrinsic the compiler lowers to the core-bundled SPI library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeWifi
    The board's Wifi: each method is a Wi-Fi intrinsic the compiler lowers to the board's networking library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NavigationListener
    Hears a Navigator's progress along its path, as leJOS's listener of the same name does.
    Navigator
    Drives a robot through a path of Waypoints, as leJOS's Navigator does: for each waypoint it turns to face the point, travels to it, and turns to the waypoint's heading when one is required.
    Navigator
    What a View uses to hand over control.
    NineAxisMotionShield
    The Bosch BNO055 orientation sensor of the Arduino 9 Axis Motion Shield, read over I2C as plain Java on top of I2c (so it needs no Arduino library).
    NoSuchAlgorithmException
    The board-side java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException.
    ObstacleDetector
    Says whether something is in the robot's way, read by a Pilot on its own thread while it travels: leJOS's FeatureDetector without the thread of its own, which a board's few thread slots cannot spare.
    Optional<T>
    The board-side java.util.Optional: the compiler reads this class as java.util.Optional, so a program written against the JDK's Optional runs this code on the board.
    OptionalLong
    The board-side java.util.OptionalLong: the compiler reads this class as java.util.OptionalLong.
    ParallelBus
    An 8-bit parallel output bus, as display shields wire it: eight data pins written together, latched by a write strobe pulsed low then high.
    PFChannel
    A channel of a Power Functions receiver, as set by its channel switch: CHANNEL_1 to CHANNEL_4.
    PFLink
    The Power Functions infrared link: the message framing and the transmission of a Power Functions command over an InfraredEmitter, as RcxLink is for the RCX.
    PFMotor
    One output of a Power Functions receiver as a DCMotor: a motor, light or servo plugged into the red or the blue port of a receiver on a channel.
    PFPort
    An output of a Power Functions receiver: the red port, also called A, or the blue port, also called B.
    Pico2WTrustZoneStore
    Named-secret storage on the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, kept by Juno's own TrustZone secure firmware: the RP2350 has no secure element, so a small program in the Cortex-M33's secure world holds the slots in a flash sector it fences off, and this program, which runs in the non-secure world, reaches them only through that firmware's one gateway.
    Pilot
    Moves a robot straight and turns it in place, as leJOS's MoveController with its rotation does: the moves a Navigator drives a path with.
    PKCS8EncodedKeySpec
    An EC private key in PKCS#8 DER form.
    Pop3Client
    A minimal POP3S client recognized as a compiler intrinsic by Juno, backed by the same board-specific implicit-TLS transport as the board's HTTPS requests.
    PortentaHatCarrier
    Pin map for the Arduino Portenta Hat Carrier (ASX00049) with a Portenta H7 on it.
    PortNoise
    Collects a best-effort startup seed from a user-provided physical noise source attached to Arduino pins.
    Pose
    Mutable, allocation-free planar pose for a differential-drive robot, Cartesian as leJOS's pose and a DirectionFinder's direction are: heading zero points along +x, the heading grows counter-clockwise, and +y is to the left of heading zero.
    PoweredUpAccelerometer
    The Technic Hub's accelerometer: gravity-compensated acceleration along X, Y and Z.
    PoweredUpBattery
    The Technic Hub's battery as the board's shared Battery interface: the hub's own charge percentage, and its supply voltage read from the hub's internal voltage sensor.
    PoweredUpGyroscope
    The Technic Hub's gyroscope.
    PoweredUpMotor
    The motor on one external port of a Powered Up hub, as an EncoderMotor.
    PoweredUpPort
    An external port of a Powered Up hub, printed on the hub as A to D: it takes a motor or an external sensor.
    PoweredUpTilt
    The Technic Hub's tilt sensor: three angles in degrees, yaw first, then pitch and roll.
    PrivateKey
    A PKCS#8 private key passed to the board TLS listener.
    Psram
    Explicit access to the board's external pseudo-static RAM (PSRAM).
    PwmServoShield
    The "16 x 12-bit PWM & Servo Shield": an NXP PCA9685 that generates sixteen servo signals on its own, driven over I2C as plain Java on top of I2c (so it needs no Arduino library).
    Random
    Pseudorandom-number operations backed by Arduino's random generator.
    RangeFinder
    A sensor that reports the distance to the nearest object.
    RangeObstacleDetector
    An ObstacleDetector over a forward-facing RangeFinder, such as a Grove Ultrasonic Ranger: blocked once confirmReadings readings in a row are nearer than stopMillimetres, and clear again only once a reading is beyond clearMillimetres or finds no echo.
    RaspberryPico2WifiBoard
    Selects the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W as @Board's target.
    RcxAudio
    An RCX brick's speaker, from RemoteRcx.getAudio().
    RcxBattery
    An RCX brick's batteries, from RemoteRcx.getBattery().
    RcxBrick
    The RCX's direct commands that answer back, the protocol under RemoteRcx's motors, sensors, display, sound and battery; use RemoteRcx in a program.
    RcxButtons
    An RCX brick's own View, Prgm and Run buttons, from RemoteRcx.getButtons().
    RcxChannel
    A Juno firmware channel of an RCX brick, or the original unchannelized broadcast.
    RcxFirmware
    Loads firmware into an RCX brick over infrared, as the LEGO IR tower does: the brick's boot ROM answers these four commands even when it has no firmware, which is the state it is in after its batteries were out (the display then shows program 0).
    RcxLcd
    An RCX brick's display, from RemoteRcx.getLcd().
    RcxLight
    A lamp connected to one of an RCX brick's motor outputs for tone activity indication.
    RcxLightSensor
    A light sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxLink
    The RCX infrared framing: a message is 55 FF 00 followed by the opcode, its arguments and a checksum, each byte followed by its complement.
    RcxMotor
    One or more of an RCX brick's outputs, driven with direct commands over infrared: get them from RemoteRcx.getMotorA(), RemoteRcx.getMotorB() and RemoteRcx.getMotorC(), and combine them with RcxMotor.and(RcxMotor) so that several outputs start and stop in the same command, e.g. the two sides of a vehicle.
    RcxMotorPort
    An output of an RCX brick, printed on the brick as A, B or C: the motor plugs in there.
    RcxRegulatedDiagnostics
    Diagnostics read from the brick for a regulated pair, for tuning and floor tests: the control-cycle counter, which gives the brick's cycle rate, and how the wheel sync drives each side.
    RcxRegulatedDifferentialDrive
    A two-wheel RCX vehicle whose wheels are regulated on the brick: one RcxRegulatedPair on the firmware's only mapping (motor A with sensor 1 as the pair's left side, motor C with sensor 3 as its right side) driven by distance and heading through a RegulatedDifferentialDrive.
    RcxRegulatedMotor
    One side of an RcxRegulatedPair, as the RegulatedMotor contract: speed and acceleration are the pair's, a rotation of this side starts a movement in which the other side stays where it is, and the tachometer is this side's own.
    RcxRegulatedPair
    The A and C outputs of an RCX regulated by its own firmware, with their rotation sensors on inputs 1 and 3, driven as one pair: a movement sets both wheels' targets in a single infrared command, and the brick regulates both on its own between commands.
    RcxRegulatedState
    The state of a regulated RCX pair, as the firmware reports it, plus two states the host itself determines: RcxRegulatedState.EXTERNAL_OVERRIDE when a manual output command took the outputs back, and RcxRegulatedState.LINK_UNKNOWN when the outcome of the last command could not be resolved over the infrared link.
    RcxRemoteControl
    A receive-only LEGO Mindstorms RCX remote control, such as the 9738 handset.
    RcxRemoteControlButton
    One of the buttons exposed by the LEGO Mindstorms 9738 RCX remote control.
    RcxRotationSensor
    A rotation sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxSensor
    One of an RCX brick's three sensor inputs: get it from RemoteRcx.getSensor1(), RemoteRcx.getSensor2() or RemoteRcx.getSensor3() and hand it to the sensor plugged into it, an RcxTouchSensor, RcxLightSensor, RcxTemperatureSensor or RcxRotationSensor, created once, at startup.
    RcxSensorPort
    A sensor input of an RCX brick, printed on the brick as 1, 2 or 3: a touch, light or rotation sensor plugs in there.
    RcxTemperatureSensor
    A temperature sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxTouchSensor
    A touch sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RegulatedDifferentialDrive
    Drives a two-wheel robot by distance and heading, with its wheels regulated by a RegulatedPair (such as an RCX pair).
    RegulatedMotor
    A motor with encoder feedback and closed-loop speed/position control.
    RegulatedPair
    Two regulated motors that start, stop and report as one unit, such as the two drive wheels of a vehicle.
    RemotePF
    A LEGO Power Functions infrared remote (8885), which drives the motors, lights and servos plugged into an IR Receiver (8884) set to one of its four channels.
    RemotePoweredUpHub
    A LEGO Powered Up hub (City Hub 88009, Technic Hub 88012, BOOST Move Hub 88006, DUPLO Train Hub, ...) controlled over Bluetooth Low Energy, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno and backed by the Arduino ArduinoBLE library (arduino-cli lib install ArduinoBLE).
    RemoteRcx
    A LEGO Mindstorms RCX brick reached over infrared: create it once, at startup, with the already-configured infrared RcxLink and a firmware channel; construction creates the brick's parts from the link — its motors (RemoteRcx.getMotorA(), RemoteRcx.getMotorB(), RemoteRcx.getMotorC()), its sensor inputs (RemoteRcx.getSensor1(), RemoteRcx.getSensor2(), RemoteRcx.getSensor3()), its display (RemoteRcx.getLcd()), its speaker (RemoteRcx.getAudio()), its batteries (RemoteRcx.getBattery()) and its firmware loader (RemoteRcx.getFirmware()).
    RplidarA2
    A Slamtec RPLIDAR A2 (A2M8) 360-degree laser scanner reached through its USB adapter, whose CP2102 bridge sits on a UsbHostShield.
    SampleProvider
    Source of sensor samples.
    SdCard
    Access to an SPI SD card, backed by the Arduino SdFat library with long-file-name support enabled.
    Se050C2
    Named-secret storage in the NXP SE050C2 used by the Portenta H7.
    SecretStore
    Named secrets kept by the board's secret store.
    SecureRandom
    The board-side java.security.SecureRandom, only as the type of SSLContext.init's last parameter, which a program passes null: the board's TLS client brings its own randomness.
    SensorMode
    One way of reading a sensor: a SampleProvider with a name, such as a temperature or a humidity mode of the same device.
    SensorModes
    A sensor with several modes.
    Serial
    USB serial output recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.
    Servo
    A zero-cost servo motor handle for a standard 3-wire hobby servo (signal, power, ground), backed by the Arduino Servo library.
    Smtp
    A minimal SMTP client recognized as a compiler intrinsic by Juno.
    SntpClock
    The SNTP server behind the internet-backed LocalDateTime.now() intrinsic, which synchronizes UTC over one UDP exchange on its own socket (separate from any socket the program opens) and then advances it with the board's millisecond counter.
    Spi
    Full-duplex SPI on the board's primary bus (SCK, MOSI and MISO).
    SSLContext
    The board-side javax.net.ssl.SSLContext: the trust a java.net.http client checks servers against, given with HttpClient.newBuilder().sslContext(context).
    Syslog
    Sends log lines as RFC 5424 syslog datagrams over UDP (RFC 5426), so a board can be followed over Wi-Fi without a USB cable; juno:monitor -Djuno.syslog=<port> receives them.
    Task
    Background work a ViewRouter advances a little every frame, before the active view renders: the single-threaded alternative to a background thread, for a board whose RAM has no room for a thread stack.
    TftTouchShield
    Driver for the ELEGOO 2.8" TFT touch screen shield ("Pantalla Táctil TFT de 2,8 pulgadas"): a 240x320 ILI9341 display on an 8-bit parallel bus, a 4-wire resistive touch panel, and a microSD socket, wired for the shield's standard UNO pinout as used by ELEGOO's Elegoo_TFTLCD and TouchScreen libraries.
    Thermometer
    A device that measures temperature, in degrees Celsius.
    TiLink
    A TI-84 Plus family calculator on the USB Host Shield, reached with its ordinary computer cable: the board plays the part of TI Connect and sends variables to the calculator over TI's USB link protocol ("DUSB"), so a program can put sensor readings into the lists L1 to L6 for a STAT PLOT.
    TouchScreen
    A touch input.
    TrustManager
    The board-side javax.net.ssl.TrustManager: what a TrustManagerFactory hands to an SSLContext.
    TrustManagerFactory
    The board-side javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory: turns a KeyStore of trusted certificates into the TrustManager an SSLContext takes.
    URI
    The board-side java.net.URI: the compiler reads this class as java.net.URI, so a program that calls URI.create(...) or new URI(...) against the JDK runs this code on the board.
    UsbHostShield
    The Arduino USB Host Shield: a Maxim MAX3421E USB host controller driven over Spi as plain Java, so it needs no Arduino library.
    UuidCodec
    Converts UUID values to and from their 16-byte, most-significant-byte-first network representation.
    View
    One screen of a multi-view program.
    ViewRouter
    The controller of a multi-view TFT program: it owns the views, runs the frame loop and switches the active view when a view asks through Navigator.
    Watchdog
    Enables the target's hardware watchdog timer on @Watchdog's entry-point class.
    Waypoint
    A point a Navigator drives to, in the pose's Cartesian millimetres, optionally with the heading the robot must face there, as leJOS's Waypoint.
    WaypointListener
    Receives a path one waypoint at a time from whatever plans it, as leJOS's interface of the same name does: a Navigator implements it, and a planner such as DetourPlanner feeds it.
    Wifi
    Wi-Fi connection control.
    WifiProvisioner
    Wi-Fi provisioning without baking credentials into the firmware, written in plain Java on top of MCU.getWifi() and the board's native HTTP listener, without a server thread (it adds no intrinsics, and costs nothing in a program that does not call it).
